Present Misc. Appeal, under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for brevity "the Act") has been preferred by the appellants/claimants assailing the award dated 18/8/2011 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sabalgarh, District Morena (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 162/2010 on the point of inadequacy of the compensation amount.

The accident in question took place on 31/01/2010 in which husband of appellant no. 1 and father of appellants No. 2 & 3 and son of appellants No. 4 and 5, namely Brijbhan sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same during treatment.
Appellants/claimants had filed the claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 35,59,000/- on account of death of husband of Appellant No.1.
However, Claims Tribunal has awarded a total copensation of Rs.4,68,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of application.

As the incident occurred, negligence of driver of driving the offending vehicle, the issue of liability have been decided recording the findings in favour of the appellants by the Tribunal and none of those findings have been assailed at the instance of the respondents i.e. owner, driver or insurance company by filing the cross-appeal or the cross-objection, it is not necessary to narrate the entire facts in detail to burden the judgment on the said issues.
It is only the inadequacy of the compensation which has been assailed, however the arguments in detail have been considered in succeeding paragraphs.

According to appellants/claimants, the tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.3,000/- per month, whereas, the deceased was engaged in labour work at a building material shop thereby used to earn Rs. 4,500/- per month and also used to earns Rs. 4,500/- by selling milk.

Further, no amount under the head future prospects in light of decision of Apex Court in the matter o f National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., 2017 ACJ 2700 has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

On the other hand, Shri Gupta learned counsel representing the respondent /Insurance Company argued in support of impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties, in the opinion of this Court, income of the deceased is required to be assessed in light of evidence came on record and legal guidance given by Apex Court.

Though appellants have claimed that deceased was doing labour work at a building material shop and also used to sell milk and thereby earning Rs. 9,000/- per month and in this regards also examined AW/2 and 3; however, in absence of any cogent evidence, the trial Court assessed the same at Rs. 3,000/- per month.

In the opinion of this Court, looking to the number of dependents upon the deceased and pleadings on record, the income of deceased as assessed by Claims Tribunal appears to be on lower side and in the facts and circumstances of the case, same is assessed at

Rs.
3,500/- per month.

The multiplier of 17 as applied by the Claims Tribunal appears to be just and proper looking to the age of deceased 35 years at the time of incident and the deduction made by Claims Tribunal at 1/4th towards self expenditure opinion of this Court is also just and proper.

Further in the opinion of this Court, the Claims Tribunal has erred in not awarding any sum under the head future prospects and since the deceased was aged 35 years at the time of incident and was engaged in non-permanent job, claimants shall be entitled to receive 40% towards future prospects on behalf of deceased.

Thus by assessing the monthly income of the deceased to Rs. 3,500/- per month, his yearly income comes to Rs. 42,000/- and after deducting 1/4th towards self expenditure, the loss of yearly dependency comes to Rs. 31,500/-, and after adding 40% towards future prospects, the yearly loss comes to Rs. 31,500/- + 12,600/- =
44,100/- and after applying multiplier of 17 as has been applied by Claims Tribunal total loss of dependency comes to Rs. 43,100 x 17 = 7,32,700/-.
The claimants shall also be entitled to receive Rs. 70,000/- towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and loss of consortium in light of decision of Apex Court in the matter of Pranay Sethi (supra).

Thus, the total compensation comes to Rs. 7,32,700/- + 70,000 =
8,02,700/-.

The Claims Tribunal has already awarded a compensation of Rs.
4,68,500/-, therefore, the claimants shall be entitled to receive an enhanced compensation of Rs. 8,02,700/- - 4,68,500/- = 3,34,200/-.

The enhanced amount of compensation to the tune of Rs. 3,34,200/- shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per Smt.Maheshwari vs Dwarika Prasad (Dead) Th: Lrs. Damodar on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117128802/
3 annum from July, 2017 when the decision of Apex Court in the matter o f Pranay Sethi (supra) came into force and for rest of the amount the conditions as imposed of Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
